clue.text: Giving up upper classes' style of expression, penning article

parts.note: AB are the top social grades in the British A, B, C1 classification

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the style word is written around the article

parts.note: diction is one's choice and delivery of words
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A snob drops their posh way of speaking, with a piece of writing in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's market-research social grades run A, B, C1 and so on, so the top two stand for the upper classes; 'penning' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdication is the act of renouncing a throne or responsibility.

clue.text: Drunk in Ireland, an exciting chemical

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reeling about and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: A night out in Dublin gives a rush of hormones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges IRELAND AN; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone released by the adrenal glands under stress stimulates the body.

clue.text: Made poet heartless

indicators.note: heartless asks for the central letter of the poet's name to be removed

parts.note: John Donne was a seventeenth-century English poet

explanation.surface: A poet was turned cold and unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle N out of DONNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done has been made or completed.

clue.text: He believes there's something due to him

definitions.text: He believes there's something due to him

parts.words: He believes there's something due to him
parts.note: reads like a man with an entitled attitude, but describes the person to whom a debt is owed

explanation.surface: A self-important man thinks the world owes him.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender is owed money by a debtor, so something is due to him.

clue.text: British computer pioneer finally abandons good foreign city

indicators.note: the good letter is dropped from the very end of the pioneer's surname

parts.note: Alan Turing pioneered computer science

explanation.surface: A famous British computing figure leaves a fine city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally abandons' drops the last letter G from TURING.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Bumper collection from vehicle

definitions.meaning: a large volume gathering several works together
an old word for a bus

explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus edition gathers many stories; an omnibus was also the horse-drawn forerunner of the bus.

clue.text: One hopes it is seen, though isle is stormy

indicators.note: stormy suggests the letters of the two words tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: A coastal tower should be visible even when the island is battered by weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is stormy' rearranges THOUGH and ISLE; the definition is a description of the building's purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal tower with a lamp exists precisely to be visible to ships.

clue.text: Irregular mass of snow in a French border

indicators.note: border used as a verb: the French article lies on either side of the snow

parts.note: UN is French for a
névé is granular snow on a glacier

explanation.surface: A rough patch of snow sits on a boundary in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' is a verb here: the French article lies on either side; 'in' is only a link. Névé is the compacted snow of a glacier's upper reaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uneven is not smooth or regular.

clue.text: Not knowing Italian, head off to get an engineer

indicators.note: the first letter of the Italian title is removed

parts.note: Signor is the Italian equivalent of Mr
CE stands for Civil Engineer

explanation.surface: A monolingual traveller drops their Italian and hires a technician instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' removes the first letter S of SIGNOR, an Italian man's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is a lack of knowledge.

clue.text: Regularly pay for right type of surgeon

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat surgery

explanation.surface: Someone pays a specialist doctor on a schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To rent something is to pay periodically for its use.

clue.text: Cry of surprise as a vehicle enters capital

indicators.note: enters means the vehicle goes between the letters of the cry and the article

parts.note: ha is an exclamation of surprise
a van is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone gasps as a lorry drives into a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' splits the cry and the article, putting the vehicle between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana is the capital of Cuba.

clue.text: Mineral available from clubs, hotel and a pub

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
an inn offers lodging like a hotel
a bar is a drinking place

explanation.surface: A rock sample is on offer at a nightspot, lodging and drinking house.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is the red ore of mercury.

clue.text: Not be the first to find dog's name round top of eating plate

definitions.text: Not be the first to find

indicators.note: round means the dog's name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Rover is a stock name for a dog

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a disc is a flat round plate

explanation.surface: A dog with a name tag sniffs around the dinner plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the dog's name around the other pieces; 'top of' takes the first letter of 'eating'. 'Not be the first to find' reads as modesty but defines finding again.
explanation.definitionFit: To rediscover something is to find it again after someone, or oneself, found it before.

clue.text: Musician putting money forward to get a title

indicators.note: putting asks for the money letter to be shifted to a new place
forward shows the money letter is shifted earlier in the composer's name

parts.note: Handel was a German-born Baroque composer
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A composer invests cash in order to gain a peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting forward' moves L one place earlier in HANDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name or title.

clue.text: Created calm

definitions.meaning: made, as of music or verse

explanation.definitionFit: A composer has written a piece; a person under control is serene.

clue.text: Beat powerfully, liking to hold end up

indicators.note: to hold means the liking word is wrapped around the turned piece

parts.note: palate means taste or liking

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tip is an end

explanation.surface: A heart pounds with fondness, hanging on until the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the end word from bottom to top; 'to hold' then puts it inside the liking word, palate in the sense of taste.
explanation.definitionFit: To palpitate is for the heart to throb rapidly and strongly.

clue.text: In panic, we hear, seize and hold reptile

indicators.note: we hear means a word is said aloud and its sound is used

parts.note: terror is extreme fear
to pin someone is to grab and hold them down

explanation.surface: In fright, someone grabs a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent TERROR sounds like TERRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle.

clue.text: Overcome by fear, having no staff present

explanation.definitionFit: Courage drained away leaves someone unnerved; a craft with no crew aboard is crewless.

clue.text: Some days, can I drink!

parts.note: MAR is March, a stretch of days
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A man wonders if he may have a cocktail on certain days.
explanation.walkthrough: MAR, the abbreviation for March, stands for 'some days' as a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth.

clue.text: Scolds as being overdue on board

indicators.note: on board in crosswords means put inside the ship's letters

parts.note: board suggests boarding a steamship, SS
being overdue means late

explanation.surface: A captain rebukes passengers for arriving late to the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' signals inside SS, the steamship abbreviation; LATE goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate someone is to criticise them harshly.

clue.text: Excessively poor quality stuff on display from military

parts.note: tat is cheap tasteless goods
too means excessively

explanation.surface: Far too much junk is shown off by the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' links; the excessive word goes last although printed first. A tattoo in this sense is a military pageant, not ink on skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a military display or pageant, such as the Edinburgh Military Tattoo.

clue.text: Little task incomplete-attempt knightly quest

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter of the task word is missing

parts.note: an errand is a small job
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A small job, half done, becomes a chivalric mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops the D from ERRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Errantry is the wandering of a knight in search of adventure.

clue.text: I'll enter part of church — simple

indicators.note: enter means the letter goes inside the church part

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
I'll is I will, giving the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone says they will walk into the body of a church, plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enter' puts I inside NAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and unsophisticated.

clue.text: In pen, write way to eating place

indicators.note: in shows that the street goes inside the pen word
write here is an instruction to put the street into the pen word

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone writes down the directions to a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In pen, write way' is an instruction: write the street abbreviation inside the ballpoint, a biro being the British word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal restaurant.

clue.text: The Chinese way is to eat cold Mexican food

indicators.note: to eat means the Chinese word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: Tao is the way in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: In China they enjoy a cold snack from Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts C inside TAO.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a folded tortilla with a filling.

clue.text: Musical performance I followed

indicators.note: followed shows the letter comes after the performance

parts.note: a gig is a live performance

explanation.surface: A show was put on and I came after.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is a stage and film musical by Lerner and Loewe.

clue.text: Wader splashes — hear a plop

indicators.note: splashes suggests letters scattered like water

explanation.surface: A bird in the shallows makes a noise as it hits the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashes' rearranges HEAR A PLOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A phalarope is a small wading bird.

clue.text: Put aside and neglect bird with difficulty

parts.note: the pigeon is a bird
being in a hole means being in difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone shelves a problem about a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeonhole a matter is to file it away and ignore it.
